claim: The expression levels of let-7 miRNA family members in naive CD8 T cells are very high.
source: Surprisingly, the initially very high expression of let-7 miRNAs in naive CD8 T cells was reduced by TCR signaling, and this downregulation was proportional to the strength and duration of TCR-stimulation, regardless of housekeeping RNA used (Figure 1A,B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states that let-7 miRNAs have 'very high expression' in naive CD8 T cells, supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1A,B.

claim: TCR signaling reduces let-7 miRNA expression in activated CD8 T cells.
source: Surprisingly, the initially very high expression of let-7 miRNAs in naive CD8 T cells was reduced by TCR signaling, and this downregulation was proportional to the strength and duration of TCR-stimulation, regardless of housekeeping RNA used (Figure 1A,B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The manuscript presents qRT-PCR data in Figure 1A,B showing dose-dependent and time-dependent reduction of let-7 expression upon TCR stimulation.

claim: The downregulation of let-7 miRNAs upon TCR stimulation is proportional to the strength of TCR stimulation.
source: Surprisingly, the initially very high expression of let-7 miRNAs in naive CD8 T cells was reduced by TCR signaling, and this downregulation was proportional to the strength and duration of TCR-stimulation, regardless of housekeeping RNA used (Figure 1A,B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Figure 1A shows dose-dependent reduction of let-7 with increasing anti-TCR antibody concentrations (0, 0.1, 0.5, 1 μg).

claim: The downregulation of let-7 miRNAs upon TCR stimulation is proportional to the duration of TCR stimulation.
source: Surprisingly, the initially very high expression of let-7 miRNAs in naive CD8 T cells was reduced by TCR signaling, and this downregulation was proportional to the strength and duration of TCR-stimulation, regardless of housekeeping RNA used (Figure 1A,B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Figure 1B shows time-dependent reduction of let-7 over increasing periods of stimulation (0, 15, 24, 48, 72 hr).

claim: miR-17 from the miR-17–92 locus is upregulated upon T cell activation.
source: As a specificity control, we confirmed the upregulation of miR-17 from the miR-17–92 locus (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B) that is induced upon T cell activation (Katz et al., 2014; Wu et al., 2012).
evidence: The manuscript presents qRT-PCR data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B and cites previous studies (Katz et al., 2014; Wu et al., 2012).

claim: P14+Lin28Tg CD8 T cells are significantly larger in size compared to P14+wild-type counterparts.
source: In comparison to the P14+wild-type counterparts, P14+Lin28Tg CD8 T cells were significantly larger in size, with a dramatically increased proportion of Ki67-positive cells (Cuylen et al., 2016) (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: Figure 1C shows FSC analysis demonstrating increased cell size in P14+Lin28Tg mice.

claim: P14+Lin28Tg CD8 T cells have a dramatically increased proportion of Ki67-positive cells compared to P14+wild-type counterparts.
source: In comparison to the P14+wild-type counterparts, P14+Lin28Tg CD8 T cells were significantly larger in size, with a dramatically increased proportion of Ki67-positive cells (Cuylen et al., 2016) (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: Figure 1D shows Ki67 expression and quantification demonstrating increased Ki67+ cells in P14+Lin28Tg mice.

claim: P14+Lin28Tg mice have a significantly higher frequency of BrdU-positive cells in both the spleen and lymph nodes compared to P14+wild-type mice.
source: Consistent with the increased proportion of Ki67-positive cells, P14+Lin28Tg mice had a significantly higher frequency of BrdU-positive cells in both the spleen and lymph nodes, as compared to P14+wild-type mice (Figure 1E).
evidence: Figure 1E shows BrdU incorporation data demonstrating increased proliferation in P14+Lin28Tg mice.

claim: Surface expression of CD122 is increased in P14+Lin28Tg CD8 T cells compared to P14+wild-type cells.
source: In addition, surface expression of T cell activation markers, such as the IL-2 receptor beta-chain (CD122), and CD44 was also increased, while cells remained CD25 negative (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: Figure 1—figure supplement 3B shows flow cytometry data and quantification of CD122 expression.

claim: Surface expression of CD44 is increased in P14+Lin28Tg CD8 T cells compared to P14+wild-type cells.
source: In addition, surface expression of T cell activation markers, such as the IL-2 receptor beta-chain (CD122), and CD44 was also increased, while cells remained CD25 negative (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: Figure 1—figure supplement 3B shows flow cytometry data and quantification of CD44 expression.

claim: P14+Lin28Tg CD8 T cells remain CD25 negative.
source: In addition, surface expression of T cell activation markers, such as the IL-2 receptor beta-chain (CD122), and CD44 was also increased, while cells remained CD25 negative (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: Figure 1—figure supplement 3B shows flow cytometry data demonstrating no significant difference in CD25 expression.

claim: The expression of let-7 miRNAs maintains the quiescent state in naive CD8 T cells.
source: Thus, these results suggest that the expression of let-7 miRNAs may maintain the quiescent state in naive CD8 T cells.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the observation that let-7 deficiency leads to increased proliferation, cell size, and activation marker expression.

claim: P14+let-7Tg CD8 T cells fail to clonally expand in response to LCMV Armstrong infection.
source: Interestingly, the recovery of donor CD8 T cells at the peak of the immune response revealed that P14+let-7Tg CD8 T cells failed to clonally expand (Figure 2B) and lacked KLRG1 expression, an established marker of terminal effector CTLs (Dominguez et al., 2015; Joshi et al., 2007; Thimme et al., 2005; Voehringer et al., 2001) (Figure 2C).
evidence: Figure 2B shows quantification of donor CD8 T cells 7 days post-infection, demonstrating reduced numbers in P14+let-7Tg mice.

claim: P14+let-7Tg CD8 T cells lack KLRG1 expression in response to LCMV Armstrong infection.
source: Interestingly, the recovery of donor CD8 T cells at the peak of the immune response revealed that P14+let-7Tg CD8 T cells failed to clonally expand (Figure 2B) and lacked KLRG1 expression, an established marker of terminal effector CTLs (Dominguez et al., 2015; Joshi et al., 2007; Thimme et al., 2005; Voehringer et al., 2001) (Figure 2C).
evidence: Figure 2C shows flow cytometry data and quantification demonstrating reduced KLRG1+ cells in P14+let-7Tg donor cells.

claim: KLRG1 is an established marker of terminal effector CTLs.
source: Interestingly, the recovery of donor CD8 T cells at the peak of the immune response revealed that P14+let-7Tg CD8 T cells failed to clonally expand (Figure 2B) and lacked KLRG1 expression, an established marker of terminal effector CTLs (Dominguez et al., 2015; Joshi et al., 2007; Thimme et al., 2005; Voehringer et al., 2001) (Figure 2C).
evidence: The manuscript cites multiple studies (Dominguez et al., 2015; Joshi et al., 2007; Thimme et al., 2005; Voehringer et al., 2001) establishing KLRG1 as a marker of terminal effector CTLs.

claim: let-7Tg CTLs have a reduced frequency of IFN-γ+TNF-α+ cytokine double-producing cells compared to wild-type CTLs.
source: Furthermore, let-7Tg CTLs had a reduced frequency of IFN-γ+TNF-α+ cytokine double-producing cells, a hallmark of an effective CD8 T cell response (Kaech et al., 2002; Wherry and Ahmed, 2004; Williams and Bevan, 2007), while the differentiation of endogenous host-derived CTLs was normal, suggesting a cell-intrinsic mechanism (Figure 2C).
evidence: Figure 2C shows flow cytometry data and quantification demonstrating reduced IFN-γ+TNF-α+ cells in P14+let-7Tg donor cells.

claim: IFN-γ+TNF-α+ cytokine double-producing cells are a hallmark of an effective CD8 T cell response.
source: Furthermore, let-7Tg CTLs had a reduced frequency of IFN-γ+TNF-α+ cytokine double-producing cells, a hallmark of an effective CD8 T cell response (Kaech et al., 2002; Wherry and Ahmed, 2004; Williams and Bevan, 2007), while the differentiation of endogenous host-derived CTLs was normal, suggesting a cell-intrinsic mechanism (Figure 2C).
evidence: The manuscript cites studies (Kaech et al., 2002; Wherry and Ahmed, 2004; Williams and Bevan, 2007) establishing this as a hallmark of effective CD8 T cell responses.

claim: The differentiation of endogenous host-derived CTLs is normal in mice receiving P14+let-7Tg donor cells.
source: Furthermore, let-7Tg CTLs had a reduced frequency of IFN-γ+TNF-α+ cytokine double-producing cells, a hallmark of an effective CD8 T cell response (Kaech et al., 2002; Wherry and Ahmed, 2004; Williams and Bevan, 2007), while the differentiation of endogenous host-derived CTLs was normal, suggesting a cell-intrinsic mechanism (Figure 2C).
evidence: Figure 2C shows that host CD45.1+ cells have normal KLRG1 and cytokine expression, indicating the effect is cell-intrinsic to the donor cells.

claim: The impaired differentiation of let-7Tg CD8 T cells is due to a cell-intrinsic mechanism.
source: Furthermore, let-7Tg CTLs had a reduced frequency of IFN-γ+TNF-α+ cytokine double-producing cells, a hallmark of an effective CD8 T cell response (Kaech et al., 2002; Wherry and Ahmed, 2004; Williams and Bevan, 2007), while the differentiation of endogenous host-derived CTLs was normal, suggesting a cell-intrinsic mechanism (Figure 2C).
evidence: The normal differentiation of host cells while donor let-7Tg cells are impaired suggests the mechanism is intrinsic to the cells expressing let-7.

claim: mRNAs of the Klrg1, Ifng and Tnfa genes are not targets of let-7 miRNAs.
source: Importantly, mRNAs of the Klrg1, Ifng and Tnfa genes are not targets of let-7 miRNAs, therefore the reduced frequencies of effector cells generated from let-7Tg CD8 T cells is not simply a result of direct suppression of effector molecule expression.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states these genes are not let-7 targets, implying bioinformatic analysis or literature review.

claim: 60% of let-7Tg mice are unable to effectively respond to and clear P815 tumor cells.
source: Interestingly, when the P815 cells were injected into wild-type or let-7Tg mice of H-2b haplotype, 60% of let-7Tg mice were unable to effectively respond to, and clear the tumor (Figure 2D).
evidence: Figure 2D shows survival curves demonstrating that let-7Tg mice have reduced survival compared to wild-type mice.

claim: At 7 days post-injection with P815 cells, wild-type mice retain on average 40 × 10^6 cancer cells in the peritoneal cavity.
source: Additionally, at 7 days post-injection, wild-type mice retained on average 40 × 106 cancer cells in the peritoneal cavity, while let-7Tg mice contained 115 × 106 cancer cells (Figure 2E).
evidence: Figure 2E shows quantification of tumor burden at day 7 post-injection.

claim: At 7 days post-injection with P815 cells, let-7Tg mice contain on average 115 × 10^6 cancer cells in the peritoneal cavity.
source: Additionally, at 7 days post-injection, wild-type mice retained on average 40 × 106 cancer cells in the peritoneal cavity, while let-7Tg mice contained 115 × 106 cancer cells (Figure 2E).
evidence: Figure 2E shows quantification of tumor burden at day 7 post-injection.

claim: CD8 T cells that maintain let-7 expression upon stimulation and differentiation have a compromised response to alloantigen.
source: We concluded that CD8 T cells that maintained let-7 expression upon stimulation and differentiation had a compromised response to the alloantigen, and thus failed to reject P815 tumor cells.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the tumor rejection and tumor burden data in Figure 2D,E.

claim: The decrease in let-7 expression upon TCR activation is necessary for the proper proliferation and differentiation of cytotoxic CD8 T cells in vivo.
source: Taken together, our results demonstrate that the decrease in let-7 expression upon TCR activation is necessary for the proper proliferation and differentiation of cytotoxic CD8 T cells in vivo.
evidence: This conclusion synthesizes the LCMV infection and tumor rejection data presented in Figure 2.

claim: let-7Tg CD8 T cells proliferate less than wild-type counterparts when activated with anti-CD3 mAbs in vitro.
source: Interestingly, let-7Tg CD8 T cells proliferated less than their wild-type counterparts, while Lin28Tg CD8 T cells exhibited enhanced proliferation (Figure 3A).
evidence: Figure 3A shows CellTrace Violet proliferation assay demonstrating reduced proliferation in let-7Tg cells.

claim: Lin28Tg CD8 T cells exhibit enhanced proliferation when activated with anti-CD3 mAbs in vitro.
source: Interestingly, let-7Tg CD8 T cells proliferated less than their wild-type counterparts, while Lin28Tg CD8 T cells exhibited enhanced proliferation (Figure 3A).
evidence: Figure 3A shows CellTrace Violet proliferation assay demonstrating enhanced proliferation in Lin28Tg cells.

claim: let-7 miRNAs negatively regulate clonal expansion of activated CD8 T cells.
source: These results indicate that let-7 miRNAs negatively regulate clonal expansion of activated CD8 T cells, which is consistent with our previous results in vivo (Figure 2B).
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the in vitro proliferation data in Figure 3A and in vivo expansion data in Figure 2B.

claim: TCR-mediated downregulation of let-7 expression is needed for successful proliferation of activated CD8 T cells.
source: Thus, we concluded that TCR-mediated downregulation of let-7 expression is needed for successful proliferation of activated CD8 T cells.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the proliferation data showing impaired proliferation when let-7 is maintained.

claim: let-7 inhibits proliferation in cancerous cells by directly targeting the mRNA of genes involved in the regulation of the cell cycle.
source: Let-7 miRNAs are well-documented tumor suppressors. It has been shown that let-7 inhibits proliferation in cancerous cells by directly targeting the mRNA of genes that are involved in the regulation of the cell cycle (Johnson et al., 2007).
evidence: The manuscript cites Johnson et al., 2007 as evidence for this established role of let-7 in cancer cells.

claim: The expression of cdc25a is suppressed in activated let-7Tg CD8 T cells compared to Lin28Tg CD8 T cells.
source: In fact, the expression of some let-7 targets such as phosphatase cdc25a (cdc25a), kinase cdk6 (cdk6), and cyclin D2 (ccnd2), was suppressed in activated let-7Tg CD8 T cells, as compared to Lin28Tg CD8 T cells where it was derepressed (Figure 3B).
evidence: Figure 3B shows qRT-PCR data demonstrating reduced Cdc25a expression in let-7Tg cells and increased expression in Lin28Tg cells.

claim: The expression of cdk6 is suppressed in activated let-7Tg CD8 T cells compared to Lin28Tg CD8 T cells.
source: In fact, the expression of some let-7 targets such as phosphatase cdc25a (cdc25a), kinase cdk6 (cdk6), and cyclin D2 (ccnd2), was suppressed in activated let-7Tg CD8 T cells, as compared to Lin28Tg CD8 T cells where it was derepressed (Figure 3B).
evidence: Figure 3B shows qRT-PCR data demonstrating reduced Cdk6 expression in let-7Tg cells and increased expression in Lin28Tg cells.

claim: The expression of ccnd2 is suppressed in activated let-7Tg CD8 T cells compared to Lin28Tg CD8 T cells.
source: In fact, the expression of some let-7 targets such as phosphatase cdc25a (cdc25a), kinase cdk6 (cdk6), and cyclin D2 (ccnd2), was suppressed in activated let-7Tg CD8 T cells, as compared to Lin28Tg CD8 T cells where it was derepressed (Figure 3B).
evidence: Figure 3B shows qRT-PCR data demonstrating reduced Ccnd2 expression in let-7Tg cells and increased expression in Lin28Tg cells.

claim: Myc expression is upregulated upon T cell activation.
source: It has been shown that let-7 may also regulate the transcription factor Myc, expression of which is upregulated upon T cell activation and is essential for CD8 T cell proliferation (Best et al., 2013; Iritani et al., 2002; Kim et al., 2009; Nie et al., 2012; Verbist et al., 2016).
evidence: The manuscript cites multiple studies (Best et al., 2013; Iritani et al., 2002; Kim et al., 2009; Nie et al., 2012; Verbist et al., 2016) establishing this fact.

claim: Myc is essential for CD8 T cell proliferation.
source: It has been shown that let-7 may also regulate the transcription factor Myc, expression of which is upregulated upon T cell activation and is essential for CD8 T cell proliferation (Best et al., 2013; Iritani et al., 2002; Kim et al., 2009; Nie et al., 2012; Verbist et al., 2016).
evidence: The manuscript cites multiple studies (Best et al., 2013; Iritani et al., 2002; Kim et al., 2009; Nie et al., 2012; Verbist et al., 2016) establishing this fact.

claim: Activated let-7Tg CD8 T cells have reduced expression of Myc compared to wild-type cells.
source: Interestingly, activated let-7Tg CD8 T cells had reduced expression of Myc, whereas let-7-deficient (Lin28Tg) CD8 T cells had increased Myc expression (Figure 3C).
evidence: Figure 3C shows qRT-PCR data demonstrating reduced Myc expression in let-7Tg cells over time.

claim: let-7-deficient (Lin28Tg) CD8 T cells have increased Myc expression compared to wild-type cells.
source: Interestingly, activated let-7Tg CD8 T cells had reduced expression of Myc, whereas let-7-deficient (Lin28Tg) CD8 T cells had increased Myc expression (Figure 3C).
evidence: Figure 3C shows qRT-PCR data demonstrating increased Myc expression in Lin28Tg cells over time.

claim: Tfap4 is a direct transcriptional target of Myc.
source: To demonstrate that Myc activity was suppressed by let-7, we also analyzed the expression of a direct transcriptional target of Myc, the transcription factor AP4 (Tfap4), which sustains Myc-mediated effects in CD8 T cells during the later stages of differentiation (Chou et al., 2014).
evidence: The manuscript cites Chou et al., 2014 as evidence for Tfap4 being a direct Myc target.

claim: Tfap4 sustains Myc-mediated effects in CD8 T cells during the later stages of differentiation.
source: To demonstrate that Myc activity was suppressed by let-7, we also analyzed the expression of a direct transcriptional target of Myc, the transcription factor AP4 (Tfap4), which sustains Myc-mediated effects in CD8 T cells during the later stages of differentiation (Chou et al., 2014).
evidence: The manuscript cites Chou et al., 2014 as evidence for this function of Tfap4.

claim: mRNA of the Tfap4 gene is not a target of let-7.
source: Although mRNA of the Tfap4 gene is not a target of let-7, the expression of Tfap4 mRNA was significantly reduced in let-7Tg CD8 T cells, and enhanced in Lin28Tg CD8 T cells (Figure 3C), suggesting that let-7 regulates Myc activity in CD8 T cells.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this, implying bioinformatic analysis or literature review.

claim: The expression of Tfap4 mRNA is significantly reduced in let-7Tg CD8 T cells.
source: Although mRNA of the Tfap4 gene is not a target of let-7, the expression of Tfap4 mRNA was significantly reduced in let-7Tg CD8 T cells, and enhanced in Lin28Tg CD8 T cells (Figure 3C), suggesting that let-7 regulates Myc activity in CD8 T cells.
evidence: Figure 3C shows qRT-PCR data demonstrating reduced Tfap4 expression in let-7Tg cells over time.

claim: The expression of Tfap4 mRNA is enhanced in Lin28Tg CD8 T cells.
source: Although mRNA of the Tfap4 gene is not a target of let-7, the expression of Tfap4 mRNA was significantly reduced in let-7Tg CD8 T cells, and enhanced in Lin28Tg CD8 T cells (Figure 3C), suggesting that let-7 regulates Myc activity in CD8 T cells.
evidence: Figure 3C shows qRT-PCR data demonstrating increased Tfap4 expression in Lin28Tg cells over time.

claim: let-7 regulates Myc activity in CD8 T cells.
source: Although mRNA of the Tfap4 gene is not a target of let-7, the expression of Tfap4 mRNA was significantly reduced in let-7Tg CD8 T cells, and enhanced in Lin28Tg CD8 T cells (Figure 3C), suggesting that let-7 regulates Myc activity in CD8 T cells.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the observation that Tfap4, a Myc target, is regulated by let-7 levels despite not being a direct let-7 target.

claim: Myc supports the proliferative burst in activated CD8 T cells through metabolic reprogramming from oxidative phosphorylation to glycolysis.
source: Another important function of Myc in activated CD8 T cells is to support the proliferative burst through the metabolic reprogramming of lymphocytes from primarily oxidative phosphorylation (resting) to glycolysis (activated), as well as through an increase in protein synthesis (Cham et al., 2008; Wang et al., 2011).
evidence: The manuscript cites Cham et al., 2008 and Wang et al., 2011 as evidence for this function of Myc.

claim: Myc supports the proliferative burst in activated CD8 T cells through an increase in protein synthesis.
source: Another important function of Myc in activated CD8 T cells is to support the proliferative burst through the metabolic reprogramming of lymphocytes from primarily oxidative phosphorylation (resting) to glycolysis (activated), as well as through an increase in protein synthesis (Cham et al., 2008; Wang et al., 2011).
evidence: The manuscript cites Cham et al., 2008 and Wang et al., 2011 as evidence for this function of Myc.

claim: The expression of glucose transporters, glycolytic enzymes, and protein synthesis enzymes is suppressed in let-7 transgenic CD8 T cells.
source: Strikingly, the expression of all tested targets was suppressed in let-7 transgenic CD8 T cells, and increased in Lin28Tg-activated lymphocytes, suggesting that let-7 expression may influence Myc-dependent metabolic reprogramming of activated CD8 T cells (Figure 3D).
evidence: Figure 3D shows qRT-PCR data for multiple metabolic genes (Glut1, Glut3, Gpd2, Pfk1, Hk2, Tpi, Pkm, Ldha, Yars) demonstrating reduced expression in let-7Tg cells.

claim: The expression of glucose transporters, glycolytic enzymes, and protein synthesis enzymes is increased in Lin28Tg-activated lymphocytes.
source: Strikingly, the expression of all tested targets was suppressed in let-7 transgenic CD8 T cells, and increased in Lin28Tg-activated lymphocytes, suggesting that let-7 expression may influence Myc-dependent metabolic reprogramming of activated CD8 T cells (Figure 3D).
evidence: Figure 3D shows qRT-PCR data for multiple metabolic genes demonstrating increased expression in Lin28Tg cells.

claim: let-7 expression influences Myc-dependent metabolic reprogramming of activated CD8 T cells.
source: Strikingly, the expression of all tested targets was suppressed in let-7 transgenic CD8 T cells, and increased in Lin28Tg-activated lymphocytes, suggesting that let-7 expression may influence Myc-dependent metabolic reprogramming of activated CD8 T cells (Figure 3D).
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the observation that let-7 levels affect the expression of known Myc targets involved in metabolism.

claim: let-7 miRNAs control the proliferation of activated CD8 T cells by modulating the expression and activity of genes involved in the regulation of the cell cycle and metabolism.
source: Taken together, these results demonstrate that let-7 miRNAs control the proliferation of activated CD8 T cells by modulating the expression and activity of genes that are involved in the regulation of the cell cycle and metabolism.
evidence: This conclusion synthesizes the data on cell cycle regulators (Figure 3B), Myc (Figure 3C), and metabolic genes (Figure 3D).

claim: The expression of the let-7 transgene in P14+ CTLs greatly diminishes their cytotoxic activity.
source: In fact, the expression of the let-7 transgene in P14+ CTLs greatly diminished their cytotoxic activity (Figure 4A).
evidence: Figure 4A shows cytotoxicity assay data demonstrating reduced target lysis by P14+let-7Tg CTLs.

claim: P14+Lin28Tg CTLs exhibit enhanced cytotoxicity compared to wild-type CTLs.
source: Alternatively, P14+Lin28Tg CTLs exhibited enhanced cytotoxicity (Figure 4A), which could be reduced by restoring let-7 expression through the induction of the doxycycline-inducible let-7 transgene in P14+let-7TgLin28Tg (4 Tg) CTLs (Figure 4B), demonstrating that let-7 deficiency, and not Lin28 overexpression, is responsible for increased cytotoxicity.
evidence: Figure 4A shows cytotoxicity assay data demonstrating increased target lysis by P14+Lin28Tg CTLs.

claim: Restoring let-7 expression in P14+let-7TgLin28Tg (4 Tg) CTLs reduces their enhanced cytotoxicity.
source: Alternatively, P14+Lin28Tg CTLs exhibited enhanced cytotoxicity (Figure 4A), which could be reduced by restoring let-7 expression through the induction of the doxycycline-inducible let-7 transgene in P14+let-7TgLin28Tg (4 Tg) CTLs (Figure 4B), demonstrating that let-7 deficiency, and not Lin28 overexpression, is responsible for increased cytotoxicity.
evidence: Figure 4B shows cytotoxicity assay data demonstrating that doxycycline-induced let-7 expression reduces cytotoxicity in 4Tg CTLs.

claim: let-7 deficiency, and not Lin28 overexpression, is responsible for increased cytotoxicity in Lin28Tg CTLs.
source: Alternatively, P14+Lin28Tg CTLs exhibited enhanced cytotoxicity (Figure 4A), which could be reduced by restoring let-7 expression through the induction of the doxycycline-inducible let-7 transgene in P14+let-7TgLin28Tg (4 Tg) CTLs (Figure 4B), demonstrating that let-7 deficiency, and not Lin28 overexpression, is responsible for increased cytotoxicity.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the rescue experiment showing that restoring let-7 in the presence of Lin28 reduces cytotoxicity.

claim: TCR-mediated downregulation of let-7 microRNAs is necessary for the acquisition of cytotoxic function in differentiating CD8 T cells.
source: Thus, we demonstrated that TCR-mediated downregulation of let-7 microRNAs is necessary for the acquisition of cytotoxic function in differentiating CD8 T cells.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the cytotoxicity assay data in Figure 4A,B.

claim: Let-7Tg CTLs have less internal complexity based on side scatter intensity than wild-type cells.
source: Let-7Tg CTLs had less internal complexity based on the intensity of side scatter (SSC) than wild-type cells, whereas Lin28Tg CD8 effector cells had significantly greater complexity (Figure 4C), suggesting a change in the number of cytotoxic granules.
evidence: Figure 4C shows flow cytometry analysis of SSC demonstrating reduced granulation in let-7Tg cells.

claim: Lin28Tg CD8 effector cells have significantly greater internal complexity than wild-type cells.
source: Let-7Tg CTLs had less internal complexity based on the intensity of side scatter (SSC) than wild-type cells, whereas Lin28Tg CD8 effector cells had significantly greater complexity (Figure 4C), suggesting a change in the number of cytotoxic granules.
evidence: Figure 4C shows flow cytometry analysis of SSC demonstrating increased granulation in Lin28Tg cells.

claim: let-7Tg CTLs contain fewer Granzyme A positive granules than wild-type CTLs.
source: Indeed, let-7Tg CTLs contained fewer Granzyme A and Granzyme B positive granules than wild-type CTLs, while Lin28Tg CTLs had more (Figure 4D).
evidence: Figure 4D shows ImageStream quantification of Granzyme A+ granules demonstrating reduced numbers in let-7Tg cells.

claim: let-7Tg CTLs contain fewer Granzyme B positive granules than wild-type CTLs.
source: Indeed, let-7Tg CTLs contained fewer Granzyme A and Granzyme B positive granules than wild-type CTLs, while Lin28Tg CTLs had more (Figure 4D).
evidence: Figure 4D shows ImageStream quantification of Granzyme B+ granules demonstrating reduced numbers in let-7Tg cells.

claim: Lin28Tg CTLs contain more Granzyme A positive granules than wild-type CTLs.
source: Indeed, let-7Tg CTLs contained fewer Granzyme A and Granzyme B positive granules than wild-type CTLs, while Lin28Tg CTLs had more (Figure 4D).
evidence: Figure 4D shows ImageStream quantification of Granzyme A+ granules demonstrating increased numbers in Lin28Tg cells.

claim: Lin28Tg CTLs contain more Granzyme B positive granules than wild-type CTLs.
source: Indeed, let-7Tg CTLs contained fewer Granzyme A and Granzyme B positive granules than wild-type CTLs, while Lin28Tg CTLs had more (Figure 4D).
evidence: Figure 4D shows ImageStream quantification of Granzyme B+ granules demonstrating increased numbers in Lin28Tg cells.

claim: The expression of let-7 controls the quantity of cytotoxic granules produced during the differentiation of CTLs.
source: These results indicated that the expression of let-7 controls the quantity of cytotoxic granules produced during the differentiation of CTLs.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the granule quantification data in Figure 4D.

claim: Granzyme A, Granzyme B, and Perforin are key cytolytic factors in cytotoxic granules.
source: Next, to determine whether let-7 expression in CTLs influences the number of granules by controlling the expression of effector molecules, gene expression of Granzyme A (Gzma), Granzyme B (Gzmb), and Perforin (Prf1), the key cytolytic factors in cytotoxic granules (Hayes et al., 1989; Lancki et al., 1991), was measured.
evidence: The manuscript cites Hayes et al., 1989 and Lancki et al., 1991 as evidence for this established fact.

claim: Let-7Tg CTLs express less mRNA for Gzma compared to wild-type cells.
source: Let-7Tg CTLs, which contained fewer cytotoxic granules, expressed less mRNA for Gzma, Gzmb, and Prf1, as compared to wild-type cells, while Lin28Tg CTLs had higher expression of these effector molecules (Figure 4E).
evidence: Figure 4E shows qRT-PCR data demonstrating reduced Gzma expression in let-7Tg cells.

claim: Let-7Tg CTLs express less mRNA for Gzmb compared to wild-type cells.
source: Let-7Tg CTLs, which contained fewer cytotoxic granules, expressed less mRNA for Gzma, Gzmb, and Prf1, as compared to wild-type cells, while Lin28Tg CTLs had higher expression of these effector molecules (Figure 4E).
evidence: Figure 4E shows qRT-PCR data demonstrating reduced Gzmb expression in let-7Tg cells.

claim: Let-7Tg CTLs express less mRNA for Prf1 compared to wild-type cells.
source: Let-7Tg CTLs, which contained fewer cytotoxic granules, expressed less mRNA for Gzma, Gzmb, and Prf1, as compared to wild-type cells, while Lin28Tg CTLs had higher expression of these effector molecules (Figure 4E).
evidence: Figure 4E shows qRT-PCR data demonstrating reduced Prf1 expression in let-7Tg cells.

claim: Lin28Tg CTLs have higher expression of Gzma, Gzmb, and Prf1 compared to wild-type cells.
source: Let-7Tg CTLs, which contained fewer cytotoxic granules, expressed less mRNA for Gzma, Gzmb, and Prf1, as compared to wild-type cells, while Lin28Tg CTLs had higher expression of these effector molecules (Figure 4E).
evidence: Figure 4E shows qRT-PCR data demonstrating increased expression of all three genes in Lin28Tg cells.

claim: The observed changes in mRNA expression of effector molecules are consistent at the protein level.
source: Moreover, the observed changes in mRNA expression of effector molecules, including Interferon-gamma (IFN-γ), were consistent at the protein level (Figure 4F,G).
evidence: Figure 4F shows flow cytometry data for Granzyme B, IFN-γ, and Granzyme A protein levels, and Figure 4G shows Western blot for Perforin.

claim: The induction of let-7 expression in P14+let-7TgLin28Tg (4 Tg) CTLs reduces the expression of effector molecules.
source: Importantly, the induction of let-7 expression in the presence of Lin28 in P14+let-7TgLin28Tg (4 Tg) CTLs reduced the expression of these effector molecules (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), again demonstrating that enhanced effector molecule expression is due to let-7 deficiency.
evidence: Figure 4—figure supplement 1 shows qRT-PCR data demonstrating reduced expression of Prf1, Gzma, and Gzmb upon doxycycline treatment in 4Tg cells.

claim: Enhanced effector molecule expression in Lin28Tg CTLs is due to let-7 deficiency.
source: Importantly, the induction of let-7 expression in the presence of Lin28 in P14+let-7TgLin28Tg (4 Tg) CTLs reduced the expression of these effector molecules (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), again demonstrating that enhanced effector molecule expression is due to let-7 deficiency.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the rescue experiment showing that restoring let-7 in the presence of Lin28 reduces effector molecule expression.

claim: let-7 miRNAs negatively regulate CTL function by preventing the expression of important cytotoxic molecules.
source: Together, these data indicate that let-7 miRNAs negatively regulate CTL function by preventing the expression of important cytotoxic molecules.
evidence: This conclusion synthesizes the data on effector molecule expression (Figure 4E,F,G) and cytotoxicity (Figure 4A,B).

claim: Typical miRNA-binding sites are found in the 3' untranslated regions (UTRs) of mRNA transcripts.
source: Although typical miRNA-binding sites are found in the 3' untranslated regions (UTRs) of mRNA transcripts (Lai, 2002; Reinhart et al., 2000; Wightman et al., 1993), we analyzed the full length mRNA of Prf1, Gzma, Gzmb, and Ifng, yet no let-7-binding sites were found.
evidence: The manuscript cites Lai, 2002; Reinhart et al., 2000; Wightman et al., 1993 as evidence for this established fact.

claim: No let-7-binding sites were found in the full length mRNA of Prf1, Gzma, Gzmb, and Ifng.
source: Although typical miRNA-binding sites are found in the 3' untranslated regions (UTRs) of mRNA transcripts (Lai, 2002; Reinhart et al., 2000; Wightman et al., 1993), we analyzed the full length mRNA of Prf1, Gzma, Gzmb, and Ifng, yet no let-7-binding sites were found.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this, implying bioinformatic analysis was performed.

claim: let-7 may indirectly regulate the expression of effector molecules by controlling transcription factors.
source: This suggested that let-7 may indirectly regulate the expression of these molecules by controlling more global regulators, such as transcription factors.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of direct let-7 binding sites in effector molecule mRNAs but observed regulation of their expression.

claim: The expression of effector molecules and cytotoxic function of CD8 T cells are tightly regulated by Eomesodermin, T-bet, Zbtb32, Runx3, Notch-1 and Blimp-1.
source: It is known that the expression of effector molecules and cytotoxic function of CD8 T cells are tightly regulated by a group of transcription factors, including Eomesodermin (Eomes), T-bet, Zbtb32, Runx3, Notch-1 and Blimp-1 (Backer et al., 2014; Pearce et al., 2003; Cho et al., 2009; Kallies et al., 2009; Rutishauser et al., 2009; Szabo et al., 2002; Shin et al., 2014).
evidence: The manuscript cites multiple studies (Backer et al., 2014; Pearce et al., 2003; Cho et al., 2009; Kallies et al., 2009; Rutishauser et al., 2009; Szabo et al., 2002; Shin et al., 2014) establishing this fact.

claim: Eomes expression on both mRNA and protein levels is reduced in let-7Tg CTLs.
source: The only transcription factor whose expression on both the mRNA and protein levels was reduced in let-7Tg CTLs, and enhanced in Lin28Tg CTLs, was Eomes (Figure 5A,B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: Figure 5A shows qRT-PCR data and Figure 5B shows flow cytometry data demonstrating reduced Eomes in let-7Tg cells.

claim: Eomes expression on both mRNA and protein levels is enhanced in Lin28Tg CTLs.
source: The only transcription factor whose expression on both the mRNA and protein levels was reduced in let-7Tg CTLs, and enhanced in Lin28Tg CTLs, was Eomes (Figure 5A,B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: Figure 5A shows qRT-PCR data and Figure 5B shows flow cytometry data demonstrating increased Eomes in Lin28Tg cells.

claim: The induction of let-7 expression in P14+let-7TgLin28Tg (4 Tg) CTLs reduces the expression of Eomes.
source: Furthermore, the induction of let-7 expression in the presence of Lin28 in P14+let-7TgLin28Tg (4 Tg) CTLs reduced the expression of Eomes (Figure 5C), demonstrating that the Lin28-mediated knockdown of let-7 miRNAs results in increased expression of Eomes in Lin28Tg CTLs.
evidence: Figure 5C shows qRT-PCR data demonstrating reduced Eomes expression upon doxycycline treatment in 4Tg cells.

claim: The Lin28-mediated knockdown of let-7 miRNAs results in increased expression of Eomes in Lin28Tg CTLs.
source: Furthermore, the induction of let-7 expression in the presence of Lin28 in P14+let-7TgLin28Tg (4 Tg) CTLs reduced the expression of Eomes (Figure 5C), demonstrating that the Lin28-mediated knockdown of let-7 miRNAs results in increased expression of Eomes in Lin28Tg CTLs.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the rescue experiment showing that restoring let-7 in the presence of Lin28 reduces Eomes expression.

claim: T-bet expression is inversely correlated with Eomes expression.
source: Of note, we also found that T-bet expression was inversely correlated with Eomes, suggesting that an Eomes-dependent mechanism may control T-bet expression (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: Figure 5A,B show that T-bet expression is increased in let-7Tg cells (where Eomes is low) and decreased in Lin28Tg cells (where Eomes is high).

claim: An Eomes-dependent mechanism may control T-bet expression.
source: Of note, we also found that T-bet expression was inversely correlated with Eomes, suggesting that an Eomes-dependent mechanism may control T-bet expression (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is inferred from the inverse correlation observed between Eomes and T-bet expression.

claim: let-7 miRNAs negatively regulate Eomes expression.
source: Thus, these results demonstrate that let-7 miRNAs negatively regulate Eomes expression.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the data showing reduced Eomes in let-7Tg cells and increased Eomes in Lin28Tg cells.

claim: There is no let-7-binding site located in the 3'UTR of Eomes.
source: Interestingly, there is no let-7-binding site located in the 3'UTR of Eomes, but rather a conserved binding motif within the open reading frame of Eomes mRNA was identified (Figure 5D; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Figure 5D shows the location of the let-7 binding site in the Eomes ORF, and Supplementary file 1 presumably contains additional details.

claim: A conserved let-7 binding motif is located within the open reading frame of Eomes mRNA.
source: Interestingly, there is no let-7-binding site located in the 3'UTR of Eomes, but rather a conserved binding motif within the open reading frame of Eomes mRNA was identified (Figure 5D; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Figure 5D shows the sequence and conservation of the let-7 binding site in the Eomes ORF between mouse and human.

claim: The 10-nucleotide mouse Eomes-let-7-binding motif is functional.
source: To determine whether this binding site is functional, the 10-nucleotide mouse Eomes-let-7-binding motif was cloned into a dual luciferase vector. The vector was then transfected into NIH 3T3 fibroblasts, which have high endogenous expression of the let-7 family members (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A,B). This resulted in a significant decrease in luciferase activity, indicating that let-7 can directly bind Eomes (Figure 5E).
evidence: Figure 5E shows luciferase assay data demonstrating reduced activity with the wild-type Eomes let-7 binding site.

claim: let-7 can directly bind Eomes mRNA.
source: To determine whether this binding site is functional, the 10-nucleotide mouse Eomes-let-7-binding motif was cloned into a dual luciferase vector. The vector was then transfected into NIH 3T3 fibroblasts, which have high endogenous expression of the let-7 family members (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A,B). This resulted in a significant decrease in luciferase activity, indicating that let-7 can directly bind Eomes (Figure 5E).
evidence: The luciferase assay data in Figure 5E demonstrates functional binding of let-7 to the Eomes sequence.

claim: When the Eomes let-7-binding site is mutated, luciferase activity is restored.
source: When this sequence was mutated, disrupting the let-7-binding site, luciferase activity was restored, confirming that let-7 microRNAs directly target Eomes mRNA (Figure 5E).
evidence: Figure 5E shows luciferase assay data demonstrating restored activity with the mutated Eomes let-7 binding site.

claim: let-7 microRNAs directly target Eomes mRNA.
source: When this sequence was mutated, disrupting the let-7-binding site, luciferase activity was restored, confirming that let-7 microRNAs directly target Eomes mRNA (Figure 5E).
evidence: The luciferase assay data showing repression with wild-type sequence and restoration with mutated sequence confirms direct targeting.

claim: T-cell specific deletion of Eomes in CTLs results in gradually decreased levels of Eomes protein.
source: T-cell specific deletion of either one or both alleles of Eomes in CTLs generated from P14+CD4Cre+Eomesflfl/wt Lin28Tg, and P14+CD4Cre+Eomesflfl/flLin28Tg T cells resulted in gradually decreased levels of Eomes (Figure 6A).
evidence: Figure 6A shows qRT-PCR and flow cytometry data demonstrating dose-dependent reduction of Eomes with increasing Cre-mediated deletion.

claim: The expression of Gzma is reduced in a manner consistent with the expression of Eomes in Eomes-deleted Lin28Tg effector cells.
source: The expression of the effector molecules Gzma, and Prf1 was reduced in a manner consistent with the expression of Eomes, where loss of Eomes ameliorated the enhanced expression of these effector molecules in Lin28Tg effector cells (Figure 6B,C).
evidence: Figure 6B shows qRT-PCR data and Figure 6C shows flow cytometry data demonstrating reduced Gzma with Eomes deletion.

claim: The expression of Prf1 is reduced in a manner consistent with the expression of Eomes in Eomes-deleted Lin28Tg effector cells.
source: The expression of the effector molecules Gzma, and Prf1 was reduced in a manner consistent with the expression of Eomes, where loss of Eomes ameliorated the enhanced expression of these effector molecules in Lin28Tg effector cells (Figure 6B,C).
evidence: Figure 6B shows qRT-PCR data demonstrating reduced Prf1 with Eomes deletion.

claim: The expression of Granzyme B is not affected by loss of Eomes expression.
source: Interestingly, the expression of Granzyme B was not affected by loss of Eomes expression, suggesting Granzyme B may be more complexly regulated through other let-7-dependent, but Eomes-independent mechanisms (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Figure 6—figure supplement 1 shows flow cytometry data demonstrating no significant change in Granzyme B with Eomes deletion.

claim: Granzyme B may be regulated through let-7-dependent, but Eomes-independent mechanisms.
source: Interestingly, the expression of Granzyme B was not affected by loss of Eomes expression, suggesting Granzyme B may be more complexly regulated through other let-7-dependent, but Eomes-independent mechanisms (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Granzyme B is regulated by let-7 but not by Eomes.

claim: The loss of Eomes expression results in a significant reduction of cytotoxic function, even in the absence of let-7 microRNAs.
source: Ultimately, the loss of Eomes expression resulted in a significant reduction of cytotoxic function, even in the absence of let-7 microRNAs (Figure 6D) while restored Eomes expression completely rescued both the cytotoxic function and the expression of effector molecules in Eomes-deficient Lin28Tg CTLs (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: Figure 6D shows cytotoxicity assay data demonstrating reduced killing with Eomes deletion in Lin28Tg cells.

claim: Restored Eomes expression completely rescues cytotoxic function in Eomes-deficient Lin28Tg CTLs.
source: Ultimately, the loss of Eomes expression resulted in a significant reduction of cytotoxic function, even in the absence of let-7 microRNAs (Figure 6D) while restored Eomes expression completely rescued both the cytotoxic function and the expression of effector molecules in Eomes-deficient Lin28Tg CTLs (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: Figure 6—figure supplement 2A shows cytotoxicity assay data demonstrating restored killing with Eomes re-expression.

claim: Restored Eomes expression completely rescues the expression of effector molecules in Eomes-deficient Lin28Tg CTLs.
source: Ultimately, the loss of Eomes expression resulted in a significant reduction of cytotoxic function, even in the absence of let-7 microRNAs (Figure 6D) while restored Eomes expression completely rescued both the cytotoxic function and the expression of effector molecules in Eomes-deficient Lin28Tg CTLs (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: Figure 6—figure supplement 2B shows qRT-PCR data demonstrating restored expression of Gzma, Gzmb, and Prf1 with Eomes re-expression.

claim: Forced expression of the mutated form of Eomes (lacking the let-7-binding motif) in let-7Tg CTLs enhances the effector phenotype.
source: Furthermore, forced expression of the mutated form of Eomes (lacking the let-7-binding motif) in let-7Tg CTLs also enhanced the effector phenotype (Figure 6—figure supplement 2C,D).
evidence: Figure 6—figure supplement 2C shows cytotoxicity assay data and Figure 6—figure supplement 2D shows qRT-PCR data demonstrating enhanced effector function and molecule expression with mutant Eomes.

claim: let-7-mediated suppression of Eomes is in part responsible for the compromised differentiation and cytotoxic function of let-7Tg CTLs in vitro.
source: These results demonstrate that let-7-mediated suppression of Eomes is in part responsible for the compromised differentiation and cytotoxic function of let-7Tg CTLs in vitro.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the Eomes deletion and rescue experiments in Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Dicer deficiency promotes the differentiation of CD8 T cells into CTLs.
source: In fact, it has been shown that Dicer deficiency promotes the differentiation of CD8 T cells into CTLs (Trifari et al., 2013), suggesting the involvement of specific miRNAs.
evidence: The manuscript cites Trifari et al., 2013 as evidence for this observation.

claim: let-7 miRNAs are the largest and most abundantly expressed family of miRNAs in CD8 T cells.
source: Let-7 miRNAs, the largest and most abundantly expressed family of miRNAs in CD8 T cells, have been shown to be important in early development, metabolism and cancer (Zhu et al., 2011; Abbott et al., 2005; Büssing et al., 2008; Roush and Slack, 2008; Yu et al., 2007).
evidence: The manuscript states this as an established fact and cites studies on let-7 function in other contexts.

claim: let-7 miRNAs have been shown to be important in early development.
source: Let-7 miRNAs, the largest and most abundantly expressed family of miRNAs in CD8 T cells, have been shown to be important in early development, metabolism and cancer (Zhu et al., 2011; Abbott et al., 2005; Büssing et al., 2008; Roush and Slack, 2008; Yu et al., 2007).
evidence: The manuscript cites multiple studies (Zhu et al., 2011; Abbott et al., 2005; Büssing et al., 2008; Roush and Slack, 2008; Yu et al., 2007) establishing this fact.

claim: let-7 miRNAs have been shown to be important in metabolism.
source: Let-7 miRNAs, the largest and most abundantly expressed family of miRNAs in CD8 T cells, have been shown to be important in early development, metabolism and cancer (Zhu et al., 2011; Abbott et al., 2005; Büssing et al., 2008; Roush and Slack, 2008; Yu et al., 2007).
evidence: The manuscript cites multiple studies establishing this fact.

claim: let-7 miRNAs have been shown to be important in cancer.
source: Let-7 miRNAs, the largest and most abundantly expressed family of miRNAs in CD8 T cells, have been shown to be important in early development, metabolism and cancer (Zhu et al., 2011; Abbott et al., 2005; Büssing et al., 2008; Roush and Slack, 2008; Yu et al., 2007).
evidence: The manuscript cites multiple studies establishing this fact.

claim: The homeostasis of naive T cells depends on the balance of recognition of low-affinity self-ligands by the TCR and cytokine stimulation.
source: It has been shown that the homeostasis of naive T cells depends on the balance of two signals, the recognition of low-affinity self-ligands by the TCR, and cytokine stimulation (Goldrath et al., 2002; Kamimura and Bevan, 2007; Kieper et al., 2004, Kieper et al., 2002; Kimura et al., 2013).
evidence: The manuscript cites multiple studies (Goldrath et al., 2002; Kamimura and Bevan, 2007; Kieper et al., 2004, Kieper et al., 2002; Kimura et al., 2013) establishing this fact.

claim: The weak recognition of self-ligands is not enough for naive T cells to lose the quiescent state.
source: Although it has become clear that the weak recognition of self-ligands is not enough for naive T cells to lose the quiescent state, the molecular mechanism that prevents the spontaneous activation of T cells under these conditions is not fully understood.
evidence: This is stated as an established fact in the field.

claim: High expression of let-7 miRNAs prevents the spontaneous activation of naive T cells.
source: Although further investigation is needed to distinguish between the let-7-dependent and let-7-independent effects of the Lin28 transgene in naive CD8 T cells, we can speculate that high expression of let-7 miRNAs prevents the spontaneous activation of naive T cells.
evidence: This is stated as speculation based on the observed phenotype of Lin28Tg naive CD8 T cells.

claim: Myc has pro-apoptotic activity.
source: Presumably due to the pro-apoptotic activity of Myc (Askew et al., 1993; Evan et al., 1992; Fanidi et al., 1992), its expression is transient, eventually receding during the later stages of CD8 T cell differentiation (Best et al., 2013; Nie et al., 2012).
evidence: The manuscript cites Askew et al., 1993; Evan et al., 1992; Fanidi et al., 1992 as evidence for this established fact.

claim: Myc expression is transient during CD8 T cell differentiation, eventually receding during the later stages.
source: Presumably due to the pro-apoptotic activity of Myc (Askew et al., 1993; Evan et al., 1992; Fanidi et al., 1992), its expression is transient, eventually receding during the later stages of CD8 T cell differentiation (Best et al., 2013; Nie et al., 2012).
evidence: The manuscript cites Best et al., 2013; Nie et al., 2012 as evidence for this observation.

claim: let-7 regulates Myc as a non-canonical target in cancer cells.
source: In our study, we have shown that let-7 suppresses the expression of Myc on the mRNA level, and consequently modulates the function of Myc in CD8 T cells, based on our assessment of established Myc targets, supporting the previous observation of Myc as a non-canonical target of let-7 miRNAs in cancer cells (Kim et al., 2009; Sampson et al., 2007).
evidence: The manuscript cites Kim et al., 2009; Sampson et al., 2007 as evidence for this previous observation.

claim: let-7 functions as a molecular rheostat that quantifies TCR signaling to direct the CTL response upon antigen stimulation.
source: We thus concluded that let-7 functions as a molecular rheostat that quantifies TCR signaling to direct the CTL response upon antigen stimulation, in a similar fashion to other miRNAs, including miR-181 and the miR-17–92 cluster (Henao-Mejia et al., 2013; Li et al., 2007; Wu et al., 2012).
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the dose-dependent and time-dependent regulation of let-7 by TCR signaling and its effects on CD8 T cell function.

claim: miR-181 functions as a molecular rheostat in T cells.
source: We thus concluded that let-7 functions as a molecular rheostat that quantifies TCR signaling to direct the CTL response upon antigen stimulation, in a similar fashion to other miRNAs, including miR-181 and the miR-17–92 cluster (Henao-Mejia et al., 2013; Li et al., 2007; Wu et al., 2012).
evidence: The manuscript cites Henao-Mejia et al., 2013; Li et al., 2007 as evidence for this function of miR-181.

claim: The miR-17–92 cluster functions as a molecular rheostat in T cells.
source: We thus concluded that let-7 functions as a molecular rheostat that quantifies TCR signaling to direct the CTL response upon antigen stimulation, in a similar fashion to other miRNAs, including miR-181 and the miR-17–92 cluster (Henao-Mejia et al., 2013; Li et al., 2007; Wu et al., 2012).
evidence: The manuscript cites Wu et al., 2012 as evidence for this function of the miR-17–92 cluster.

claim: In neonatal mice, residual expression of Lin28B in T lymphocytes skews CD8 T cell differentiation toward an effector phenotype.
source: These conclusions are supported by a recent study demonstrating that in neonatal mice the residual expression of Lin28B in T lymphocytes skews CD8 T cell differentiation toward an effector phenotype (Wang et al., 2016).
evidence: The manuscript cites Wang et al., 2016 as evidence supporting their conclusions.

claim: Eomes is only part of the cytotoxic program in CD8 T cells.
source: However, our data also suggest that Eomes is only a part of this 'cytotoxic program', as deletion of Eomes only reduced cytotoxicity to the levels exhibited by wild-type CTLs, and re-expression of Eomes in let-7Tg CTLs only marginally increased cytotoxicity.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the observation that Eomes deletion doesn't completely abolish enhanced cytotoxicity in Lin28Tg cells.

claim: Other let-7-dependent, but Eomes-independent mechanisms contribute to CTL cytotoxicity.
source: These results indicate that other let-7- dependent, but Eomes-independent mechanisms are at play.
evidence: This is inferred from the incomplete rescue of cytotoxicity by Eomes manipulation.

claim: Granzyme A is a probable target of Eomes.
source: Additionally, we have identified Granzyme A as a probable target of Eomes, while also confirming that Perforin, and IFN-γ expression is controlled by Eomes (Pearce et al., 2003).
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the observation that Granzyme A expression correlates with Eomes levels in the deletion experiments.

claim: Perforin expression is controlled by Eomes.
source: Additionally, we have identified Granzyme A as a probable target of Eomes, while also confirming that Perforin, and IFN-γ expression is controlled by Eomes (Pearce et al., 2003).
evidence: The manuscript cites Pearce et al., 2003 and presents data showing Perforin expression correlates with Eomes levels.

claim: IFN-γ expression is controlled by Eomes.
source: Additionally, we have identified Granzyme A as a probable target of Eomes, while also confirming that Perforin, and IFN-γ expression is controlled by Eomes (Pearce et al., 2003).
evidence: The manuscript cites Pearce et al., 2003 and presents data showing IFN-γ expression correlates with Eomes levels.

claim: Eomes and T-bet exhibit reciprocal expression.
source: We also observed previously reported reciprocal expression between T-bet and Eomes (Intlekofer et al., 2005; Chang et al., 2014; Nayar et al., 2012).
evidence: The manuscript cites Intlekofer et al., 2005; Chang et al., 2014; Nayar et al., 2012 and presents data showing inverse correlation.

claim: Downregulation of let-7 upon TCR stimulation is a critical process in determining the magnitude of the CD8 T cell response in vivo.
source: These results clearly demonstrate that downregulation of let-7 upon TCR stimulation is a critical process in the determination of the magnitude of the CD8 T cell response in vivo, as let-7 miRNAs inhibit proliferation and differentiation by targeting cell cycle regulators, affecting metabolic reprogramming through the suppression of Myc, and repression of effector function through Eomes-dependent and -independent mechanisms.
evidence: This conclusion synthesizes all the major findings of the study.

claim: let-7 miRNAs act as a molecular control hub that drives CD8 T cell differentiation and function in a manner dependent on the magnitude of TCR stimulation.
source: Thus, our data suggest a model in which the let-7 miRNAs act as a molecular control hub that drives CD8 T cell differentiation and function, in a manner dependent on the magnitude of TCR stimulation (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is the main model proposed by the study, synthesizing all findings and illustrated in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: Modulation of let-7 miRNA expression in CD8 T cells provides a novel therapeutic application to control CTL responses.
source: Furthermore, we propose that modulation of let-7 miRNA expression in CD8 T cells provides an exciting, novel therapeutic application to control CTL responses.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal based on the findings of the study.

claim: Naive CD8 T cells require let-7 miRNAs to remain quiescent.
source: Thus, naive CD8 T cells require let-7 miRNAs to remain quiescent, and only upon antigen stimulation through the TCR can this molecular 'brake' be released.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the observation that let-7 deficiency leads to loss of quiescence in naive CD8 T cells.

claim: let-7 acts as a molecular brake controlling the magnitude of CD8 T cell responses.
source: Ultimately, we have identified a novel let-7-mediated mechanism, which acts as a molecular brake controlling the magnitude of CD8 T cell responses.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, synthesizing all findings.
